approval_required_for: Any architecture or pipeline topology change beyond the checked Stage 3/Stage 4 structure.
Any model shape or semantics change, including hidden_size, intermediate_size, seq_len, head_dim, num_q_heads, num_kv_heads, operator order, residual paths, or branch dataflow.
Any numeric-policy change to dtype, cast points, accumulator precision, residual_precision=32, rounding, saturation, RMSNorm epsilon, or comparison tolerance.
Any rebinding of lanes, tile sizes, datapath widths, AXI packing assumptions, stream order, edge dtype widths, FIFO ownership, or global-versus-per-stage parameter precedence.

Any concrete memory layout decision or change, including DDR base addresses, address ranges, channel partitioning, non-overlap policy, 64-byte alignment interpretation, runtime ABI assignment, or transfer externalization policy.
Any major template family replacement, new semantic template parameter, or implementation repair beyond trusted template parameters and bounded glue code.
Any board/app-shell target, shell clock, or deployment binding chosen from ambiguous evidence.
Any attempt to promote timing, resource, hardware, runtime, or board-pass claims must be backed by required real tool evidence; approval cannot substitute for the named checkers.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block promotion; create an explicit bounded retry, backtrack, or trust-barrier record naming the failed checker, violated SACG constraint, and contaminated artifact boundary. Do not let downstream stages consume the unpromoted artifact.
executable_actions.rationale: The stage passed and SACG memory truth has no active blockers, so the flow controller should promote only the checker-backed Stage 4 static parameter-binding contract while recording that symbolic estimates are not hardware evidence.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the handoff pending and prevent code_generation or memory/runtime agents from consuming conflicting downstream artifacts until duplicate ownership and acceptance responsibilities are resolved.
executable_actions.rationale: The team aggregate is ready but contains overlapping memory/runtime and later-stage handoff actions. Normalize ownership and ordering so peer agents consume one coherent handoff without treating later obligations as current-stage blockers.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not modify golden outputs, loosen tolerance, or change model dimensions, numeric policy, lanes, tiles, stream order, FIFO semantics, or template semantics without approval. Localize to codegen/template binding and route to bounded repair.
executable_actions.rationale: Start the next available stage by generating code only under the promoted Stage 4 contract: per-stage parameter precedence, lanes=8, dtype/cast plan, residual_precision=32, FIFO authority, stream_order token/tile/lane/word, and numeric policy must be preserved.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep memory/runtime, verification, backend, and board promotion blocked. Localize to address map, alignment, non-overlap, ABI, or transfer-count mismatch; route to memory_runtime_repair and require approval for any memory-layout, architecture, or parameter rebinding change.
executable_actions.rationale: The parameter_binding bandwidth estimate is symbolic; the next-stage plan must assign concrete memory regions and runtime ABI only under explicit approval while preserving 512-bit AXI packing, 64-byte alignment, non-overlap, stream order, branch precision, and transfer counts.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not promote to the next hierarchy layer. Convert tool output into contract-guided localization at the earliest causal boundary, apply bounded repair, and rerun the failed layer before any higher-layer, backend, timing, or board claim.
executable_actions.rationale: Static Stage 4 and codegen checks cannot prove functional correctness, numeric equivalence, data order, liveness, or AXI/DDR protocol behavior. Later verification must run the required leaf-to-single-layer-to-board-wrapped hierarchy and stop at the first failed layer.

executable_actions.on_failure: Use the real tool output for contract-guided localization and bounded repair. Do not claim timing/resource pass, loosen numeric tolerance, modify golden outputs, or skip required verification layers.
executable_actions.rationale: Resource, timing, and implementation feasibility remain unproven until real Vivado synthesis and implementation reports are collected after static codegen, memory/runtime, and verification gates pass.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep runtime bitstream and board runtime blocked until target, shell clock, and interface binding are supported by cited evidence or explicit approval.
executable_actions.rationale: The Stage 4 artifact supplies AXI facts but not a proven app-shell target or shell clock. Backend discovery must cite real board/Vivado evidence, and ambiguous target or clock evidence requires bounded approval rather than guessed names.
